newsitem.title: USA: Hedstrom buying Ero in $203 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Hedstrom buying Ero in $203 million deal.

text.p: Hedstrom Corp., a leading maker of outdoor play equipment, has agreed to buy Ero Inc. -- whose broad line of children's products include water sports equipment -- in a deal valued at about $203 million, Hedstrom's owner said Friday.

Under terms of the deal, Hedstrom will pay $11.25 a share in cash, or about $123 million, for Ero stock and refinance Ero's debt of about $80 million, leveraged buyout firm Hicks, Muse, Tate and Furst Inc. said in a statement.
Ero stock rose 75 cents to $11 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market, topping its 52-week high of $10.625.
The buyout firm's managing director said the acquisition was the first major step in a strategy of buying children's indoor and outdoor play equipment businesses.
Mount Prospect, Ill.-based Ero's board unanimously approved the deal and recommended approval by shareholders, Dallas-based Hicks, Muse said.
Ero's largest shareholder -- the private investment firm of Golder, Thoma, Cressey, Rauner Inc. -- favours the merger, Hicks, Muse said. Golder, Thoma owns about 38 percent of Ero common stock.
The stock portion of the deal calls for Hedstrom to buy the 10.3 million outstanding shares of common stock for $11.25 a share plus 1.45 million options for Ero stock with a strike price of $6.50.
Ero has four subsidiaries and plants in Montreal and Hazelhurst, Ga.

In addition to making water sports equipment, Ero makes arts, crafts and activities products. It also sells a broad line of school supplies -- including backpacks, book bags, lunch kits, luggage, fanny packs and locker bags -- and stationery, such as portfolios, study kits, pencils and theme books.
The company had net income of $7.76 million on sales of $157.9 million in 1996.
Hedstrom, based in Pittsburgh and founded in 1915, makes and sells swing sets, wooden gym kits and slides, play balls and other outdoor products. Its factories are in Bedford, Pa., and Ashland, Ohio.
Privately owned Hedstrom did not give its sales or profit figures.
Hedstrom was bought by Hicks, Muse in 1995.

"When we acquired Hedstrom in October 1995, we believed that it would be an excellent platform from which to make further acquisitions in the children's indoor and outdoor play equipment businesses," Hicks Muse Managing Director Alan Menkes said in a statement.

"The combination of these two fine companies, Hedstrom and Ero, is the first major step in that process and is consistent with our buy-and-build philosophy," said Menkes, who also sits on Hedstrom's board.
"There are some (deals) we are looking at, but none we can talk about," Hicks, Muse Vice President Andrew Rosen said in a telephone interview.

The firm's properties also include radio and televison stations, cable televison operations in South America, International Wire Group, connector company Berg Electronics Corp. and printed circuit board maker ViaSystems.
Ero Chairman D. Richard Ryan Jr. said in the statement that the merger "represents a great opportunity for both companies to become a more important factor in children's leisure products."
